text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SmartRoutingFallback alert — health-check flap detected across regions (us-west <-> us-east <-> eu). Observed start: 2025-10-15T22:07:14Z. Symptoms: repeated region failover loop, model-variant fallback churn, increased 5xx and latency spikes. Paging on-call.

alex: i'm on it. seeing healthcheck toggles for us-west-lb-2 every ~12s in the metrics. K/V cache flushes -> cold starts -> fallback to smaller model variant.

maria: noted — customers A and B reporting slow responses and occasional empty completions. Do we have request IDs?

alex: pulling logs now. example request id: req_9f3c7a. curl healthcheck to node: `curl -fsS http://us-west-lb-2/health || echo FAIL` returns FAIL then PASS. attaching short log:
```
2025-10-15T22:06:58Z healthcheck FAIL node=us-west-lb-2 reason="socket timeout"
2025-10-15T22:07:10Z healthcheck PASS node=us-west-lb-2 latency=12ms
2025-10-15T22:07:22Z healthcheck FAIL node=us-west-lb-2 reason="backend busy"
```

kai: that looks like transient overload on the us-west pool. Could be autoscaler thrashing or a kernel OOM kill on a worker. ops-eng, can you check infra events?

ops-eng: checking. there's a flurry of GPU pod restarts on us-west yesterday after a kernel driver update we rolled out. dont see the full rollback yet.

maria: impact assessment: error-rate baseline 0.3% -> now 6.1% for text-generation endpoint. Latency p95 from 220ms -> 1.4s. A subset of heavy customers (ids c-17, c-42) saw timeouts and retried -> increased load.

alex: quick mitigation options: 1) Temporarily disable smart-routing fallbacks to stop region oscillation (will stick to primary region until manual change). 2) Pin users to stable model variant (no fallback). 3) Take us-west out of rotation via routing pool weight 0.

maria: i'd prefer option 3 + throttling new requests to us-west, then rollback driver update. Option 1 could mask real capacity issues and cause higher latency for users pinned to us-west.

kai: if we set fallback policy to prefer region staying-for-n seconds, we can prevent immediate bounce. Config looks like this: 
```
fallback_policy:
  mode: smart
  min_stay_seconds: 300
  max_retries: 2
  fallback_variants: ["small-quant", "cpu-serve"]
```
But that is a config change and might need a deploy.

alex: i'm going to set us-west pool weight=0 for the router to drain new traffic. Applying now.

incident-bot: action logged by alex at 2025-10-15T22:11:02Z — route weight us-west=0.

alex: confirmed: router reports us-west weight=0. Traffic rebalanced to us-east primary. p95 dropped to 480ms within 60s. error-rate dropped to 2.1% but still above baseline.

maria: can you also pin heavy customers to us-east until we stabilize? Put a strict route rule for c-17,c-42.

alex: done. rule added: `route: if customer in [c-17,c-42] -> region: us-east pin: true`.

ops-eng: infra notes: we see 18 GPU pod restarts in us-west over last 20m; dmesg shows GPU driver tracebacks. rolling back kernel driver to previous revision recommended. i'll start rollback; ETA 15-20m.

kai: while rollback happening, recommend increasing healthcheck retry window to avoid flapping detection: `healthcheck.interval=10s, healthcheck.failure_threshold=3` so we require 30s of consecutive fails.

alex: applied healthcheck config change on load-balancer: interval=10s, threshold=3.

incident-bot: config change recorded by alex at 2025-10-15T22:18:45Z.

support-bot: postmortem note: customers affected list: c-17, c-42, c-90 (partial), internal test traffic. No data exfiltration, only availability/latency impact.

maria: summarizing customer impact for ops email: window 22:07 -> 22:24 UTC, p95 peaked 1.4s, error-rate peak 6.1%, approx 1200 requests failed (500s), most retried. We'll offer credits if SLA breached.

ops-eng: rollback complete on driver to previous stable version on us-west at 22:26. nodes are stabilizing, pod restarts stopped.

alex: healthchecks observed PASS steady for 3 consecutive intervals. re-enabling us-west weight slowly to 0.5.

incident-bot: change logged by alex at 2025-10-15T22:28:31Z — us-west weight=0.5.

maria: keep an eye — do not re-enable fallback policy yet. we'll let routing stay conservative for 30m to verify stability.

kai: also recommend creating an automatic guard: if a region flips health state >3 times in 5m, pause fallback policy and create a direct alert to infra-sre. Could add a circuit-breaker to avoid oscillation.

alex: creating ticket for circuit-breaker feature — infra backlog. ticket id: RB-4521.

incident-bot: incident severity set to Sev2. Handoff: alex will monitor for 30m then hand off to maria for follow-up and customer comms.

maria: i'm taking over monitoring and will draft the incident summary for postmortem. Thanks alex + ops-eng + kai.

alex: handing off now, i'll be offline in 25m. leave any followups here. :thumbsup:

support-bot: automated customer status update queued — message to customers affected scheduled in 10m.

maria: closing notes for thread: root cause = GPU driver regression causing pod restarts -> healthcheck flapping -> smart-routing fallback loop. Mitigations = take region out of rotation, rollback driver, increase healthcheck thresholds, add temporary customer pinning. Action items: RB-4521 (circuit-breaker), RB-4522 (routing policy testing), customer credits assessment.

incident-bot: incident acknowledged closed for now at 2025-10-15T22:38:09Z. Reopen if flapping resumes.
